main_body: Two stacked wooden crates. Each has a light plank-striped lid on top and a dark brown front face with a diagonal brace.
top_band: Column x=15: light tan plank-striped band (L 146/113 alternating), rows 0-8, with a dark line at row 9 (L=44) before the front face.
evidence: The lid is a wide, clearly lighter horizontal surface of 9 rows. A dark 1-row step at row 9 (L=44) then leads into a much darker front face (L=65, rows 10-16), so lid and front read as two separate surfaces. The dark row acts as an eave shadow. There is no distinct lighter front-edge line, and the diagonal brace is painted flat rather than inset. The lid is tall relative to the front, but it still reads as a horizontal plank top, so the drawing passes as 3/4.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours against 40 and 38 in the references, and a median of 6 colours per tile against 17 and 20. Each material has about 3 steps: tan 146/113/88, brown 65/44/26. The lid has only a regular stripe pattern, and the front face is a nearly flat dark brown with a single diagonal brace line, so it lacks the grain, per-plank highlights and speckle the references show. The outline is tinted dark brown (12% neutral), which is fine. Overall it looks thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references.
